text:
anna: Noticed a weird jump in the dashboard p95 for /v1/generate after yesterday's routing policy tweak. p50 looks steady but p95 and p99 moved up ~80ms for one endpoint slice. Anyone else see provenance change?

matt: Yeah I saw that too. Wondering if the rollup switched from 'direct' samples to 'fallback' samples after the weight bump.

sasha: Could be sampling origin, or the merge mode changed. Can you paste the endpoint + route tags?

anna: route=customer-a, variant=redwood-v2, region=us-west. Console legend still shows single line and doesn't surface sample origin.

lucy: I can repro in the console. p50 stable, p95 drifting on that route-only slice. Looking at raw logs KV cache hit ratio didn't change much.

matt: Quick check — run this query in telemetry to see sample origins:

```
SELECT sample_origin, quantile(0.95)(latency_ms) as p95, count() as n
FROM latency.events
WHERE route='customer-a' AND variant='redwood-v2' AND region='us-west'
GROUP BY sample_origin
```

sasha: If that shows fallback has worse tail, it's probably because fallback requests hit a different model variant with longer init paths.

anna: Ran it — results: [direct: p95=120ms n=6.2k], [fallback: p95=210ms n=420]. So fallback is the culprit even though it's low volume.

lucy: That explains why p50 unchanged. But the dashboard percentiles are attributed to the merged rollup without an origin breakdown, which makes it look like overall latency regressed. UX problem.

matt: Can we add a small provenance badge on the legend when sample_origin is heterogeneous? Something like "mix: direct(94%), fallback(6%)" and hover to expand.

sasha: Good idea. Also we need to make SLA derivation explicit — right now SLO alerting uses the merged p95. So a tiny fallback bump can trigger noisy alerts for teams that only care about direct traffic.

anna: +1 — that was the pager. SLO vs derived-SLO mismatch is the immediate pain. We should have an option in the SLO config to choose attribution mode: merged|direct-only|fallback-aware.

lucy: Quick mitigation: we can add an annotation to the dashboard showing "sample_origin_pressure: true" whenever fallback contribution > 3% and p95 delta > 30ms.

matt: I'll file a short RFC for console and SLO model changes. Will include suggested legend UI and SLO config knob.

sasha: Also a runtime change: can we tag requests that hit fallback with a shorter synthetic KV cache TTL so their distribution doesn't pollute long-running aggregates? Might be heavy-handed.

anna: For immediate ops: can we surface sample counts in the heatmap tooltip? That would have helped triage without running telemetry queries.

lucy: Agree. I'll add a small ticket for heatmap tooltip + legend badge.

matt: Filed: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3210 (console: sample-origin badge + SLO attribution option).

sasha: Deploy-bot FYI — we rolled a tiny routing policy yesterday at 22:13 UTC that bumped fallback weight from 0.5% to 6% temporarily for resilience test.

deploy-bot: @channel deploy INF-routing/v1 succeeded at 2024-10-15T22:13:02Z :rocket:

anna: That matches timing. Thanks for the pointer — will follow up with the SRE team to avoid parity surprises.

lucy: Action items: matt RFC, lucy ticket for tooltip/badge, anna follow up with SRE, sasha propose runtime tagging experiment.

matt: I'll also add a small note to the rollout checklist: "check sample_origin distribution before changing fallback weight >1%".

anna: Thanks all — this saved us a noisy pager. We'll iterate on UX and SLO config next week. :thumbsup:
